titre: The Hippocampus of London Taxi Drivers
accroche: Memorizing 25,000 London streets changes the shape of part of the brain: a team measured it, then proved it was not the other way around.
contenu_vulgarise:
Becoming a London black cab driver requires passing the Knowledge, an exam that demands memorizing about 25,000 streets within a six-mile radius of Charing Cross, along with the most direct routes between them. Preparation takes three to four years on average. More than half of the candidates fail or drop out.

## A Hippocampus That Changes Shape

In 2000, the neuroscientist Eleanor Maguire and her team, at University College London, use structural MRI to compare sixteen experienced taxi drivers with fifty control subjects. The result: the rear part of the hippocampus, a region associated with spatial memory, is significantly larger in the drivers, and this volume increases with the number of years spent behind the wheel. The front part of the hippocampus, meanwhile, is slightly smaller in the drivers than in the controls.

The study makes a stir, but it has a limit it cannot lift on its own: a correlation is not proof of cause. Nothing rules out, in theory, that people who already have a more developed posterior hippocampus choose this job more readily, without driving having anything to do with it.

## Proof by Follow-Up

In 2011, Katherine Woollett and Eleanor Maguire settle the question another way: they scan seventy-nine Knowledge candidates with MRI before the start of their training, then fifty-nine of them three to four years later, alongside thirty-one controls who never undertook this preparation. Forty-one of the seventy-nine candidates, a little over half, pass the exam and obtain their license, thirty-nine of them among the fifty-nine rescanned.

Only these successful candidates show, on the second MRI, a measurable increase in gray matter in the posterior hippocampus. Neither the candidates who failed nor the controls display any change at all. The conclusion this time is unambiguous: it is sustained learning of navigation that remodels the structure of the adult brain.

## What This Shifts

For a long time, the structure of the adult brain was thought to be relatively fixed, able to learn without physically changing. The case of London taxi drivers shows the opposite: a sufficiently intense and prolonged cognitive effort leaves a measurable trace, within a few years, in the very anatomy of the brain that produced it. The gain is not free, moreover: the slight reduction observed at the front of the hippocampus suggests a trade-off rather than a simple surplus. This is a plasticity that was thought, until then, to be reserved for the child's brain.

repere.texte: Of seventy-nine candidates at the start, fifty-nine rescanned with MRI after their training, only the thirty-nine who passed the Knowledge exam showed an increase in gray matter in the posterior hippocampus, with no change in those who failed or in the controls.
repere.source: Woollett, K. & Maguire, E.A., Current Biology, 2011

carte.punch: In London taxi drivers, the back of the hippocampus grows with the years on the job.
carte.idee: Sixteen London taxi drivers have a posterior hippocampus larger than average, in proportion to their years of experience. A later follow-up confirmed the cause: among candidates followed during their training, only those who passed the exam saw this area grow.
carte.source_courte: Maguire et al., PNAS, 2000 · Woollett & Maguire, 2011

pour_aller_plus_loin.titre: Acquiring 'the Knowledge' of London's layout drives structural brain changes
pour_aller_plus_loin.note: The 2011 longitudinal study, full text in open access.

quiz.question: How did the 2011 study prove that the taxi drivers' training, and not a predisposition, causes the change observed in the hippocampus?
choix: By comparing twins of whom only one had become a taxi driver
By following the same candidates with MRI before and after training, and noting that only those who passed changed
By measuring the hippocampus of retired drivers to see whether it shrank
By comparing taxi drivers with bus drivers on the same route
quiz.explication: The 2000 study established only a correlation: nothing ruled out that people who already had a more developed posterior hippocampus chose this job more often. The 2011 longitudinal follow-up, with MRI before and after training, settled it: only the candidates who passed showed a change, not those who failed or the controls.

quiz_supplementaire.question: How many candidates are followed in the 2011 study, and how many pass the exam?
choix: Sixteen candidates followed, of whom eight passed
Seventy-nine candidates followed, of whom forty-one passed
One hundred candidates followed, half of whom passed
Fifty candidates followed, of whom twenty passed
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The 2011 study follows seventy-nine Knowledge candidates, of whom forty-one, a little over half, pass the exam and obtain their license; thirty-nine of them are rescanned.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What trade-off does the slight reduction observed at the front of the drivers' hippocampus suggest?
choix: That the gain in spatial memory comes at the expense of another function, rather than being a simple surplus
That drivers lose part of their long-term memory
That the effect reverses completely after retirement
That only men show this reduction, not women
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The slight reduction observed at the front of the hippocampus suggests a trade-off rather than a simple surplus: the gain in spatial memory at the back would not be free.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Knowledge, the exam for London black cab drivers, require?
choix: Passing a timed driving test on a closed course
Earning a university degree in urban geography
Memorizing about 25,000 streets within a six-mile radius of Charing Cross
Speaking at least two foreign languages fluently
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The Knowledge requires memorizing about 25,000 streets within a six-mile radius of Charing Cross and the most direct routes between them, preparation that takes three to four years on average.
